law: The Electron/Chromium 'husk' in this corpus comes from the depth cap, not from a renderer that has not loaded yet. The default depth-10 tree is an exact prefix of the later depth-40 tree, and all of the extra nodes hang below depth-10 frontier nodes.
evidence: Default full.json vs forced.json, matched by child-index path + role: Notion 19/19 paths match, and 985 of 985 new nodes sit under 3 frontier nodes. Claude 19/19, 17/17 under the frontier. Brave 56/56, 114/114. Firefox 93/93, 178/195. YT Music 415/437, 540 of +538. Discord: an index shift at the webarea gives a 13/25 path match, but 481 of the 482 new nodes hang off the one node whose default children_count was 2 (forced has 2 kids there). Every frontier's children_count equals the forced child count exactly: Notion 6/4/1 -> 6/4/1, Brave 10/5 -> 10/5, Firefox 9 of 9. Node counts at depth <=10, default vs forced: Discord 25 vs 27, Notion 19/19, Claude 19/19, Brave 56/56, Chrome 51/51, Firefox 93/96, YT Music 437/435. So nothing near the top 'filled in' between captures. agent-desktop 0.8.1 source (crates/macos/src/tree/query/mod.rs:59, traversal.rs:111-117) sends AXManualAccessibility only when the tree is complete, has NO webarea, and ended above --max-depth. All 8 web-stack default captures contain a webarea and reach depth 10, so that gate was false on both counts. Notion, which the census called 'veiled, handshake untested', is 1004 nodes (369 named inside its webareas) at depth 40.
exceptions: Chrome can't be tested: forced captured a different window (w-28546 vs w-28145), with 9/51 paths matching. The pre-activation captures were overwritten by capture.py, so a Chromium AX mode enabled by an earlier query cannot be ruled out. It is also not needed to explain the data.
deterministic_rule: If the tree has a webarea and any node where children_count > len(children), or the max serialized depth equals --max-depth, don't activate or wait. Recapture the same window with --max-depth 40, or run snapshot --root on each frontier ref_id. Treat 'handshake hydration' as unproven. Expect the recapture to be a strict superset of the shallow tree.
confidence: high (5 exact-prefix apps + Discord frontier match; Chrome excluded)

law: A husk-detection predicate built on the depth frontier and tiny-tree size separates untrustworthy default captures perfectly. The census predicate (offscreen present and fewer than 4 names) misses 8 of 10.
evidence: Label = forced/default node ratio >= 1.3, or opaque, or overflow. Positives (10): Discord 20.3x, Notion 52.8x, Claude 1.89x, Chrome 1.35x, Brave 3.04x, Firefox 3.10x, YT Music 2.23x, Keynote 76.6x, Antigravity (RefMap overflow), Telegram (1-node opaque). Negatives (12): Calendar, Finder, Gemini, Word, Notes, Reminders, Safari, TextEdit, UTM, VLC, WhatsApp, Zoom (ratios 0.66-1.05; the highest negative is 1.05, so the threshold has a clean gap). Predicate P = any children_count > len(children) OR node count <= 12: TP 10, FP 0, FN 0, so precision 1.0 and recall 1.0. The frontier half fires on 8 apps, all with max depth exactly 10; all 12 negatives stop at depth <= 9. The n <= 12 half catches Keynote (9) and Telegram (1). Census predicate (capture.py is_husk): TP 2 (Discord, Claude), FP 0, FN 8, recall 0.20. 'No named node inside webarea': recall 0.70 (misses Firefox 8 named, YT Music 215, Antigravity 2). Adding 'complete=false' as a husk signal adds 2 FPs (Finder, Reminders).
exceptions: 22 labeled apps is a small sample. OBS (no forced capture) and Music (forced.json is really YT Music) are excluded. Skeleton captures always have frontiers by design (--skeleton adds children_count), so run P only on full, non-skeleton snapshots.
deterministic_rule: untrusted(snapshot) := exists node with (children_count or 0) > len(children) OR total_nodes <= 12 OR (root.subtree_truncated AND ref_count == 0). Evaluate on a non-skeleton snapshot taken with a known --max-depth. Do not use offscreen counts or name counts as husk signals.
confidence: high on this corpus (10/10, 0 FP); medium for generalization

law: An exact husk fingerprint exists. Every Chromium-family app (Electron and Chromium browsers) gives the same 7-node skeleton, and its depth-10 full tree is a fixed 'traffic lights + wrapper chain + focused webarea' shape. Offscreen nodes in a husk are zero-height geometry, not hidden windows.
evidence: Skeleton: exactly 7 nodes, 5 unnamed (71%), root with 4 children, 1 hidden child, max depth 3. That holds in 6/6 Chromium-family apps (Antigravity, Brave, Claude, Discord, Chrome, Notion) and 0/16 others. The smallest others are Telegram 1, Keynote 9, and YT Music/WhatsApp/Music 11; Firefox (Gecko) is 37. Full, depth 10: the root always has 4 kids, which are 3 unnamed 16x16 buttons plus one group chain. The webarea sits at depth 7-8 with state 'focused'. Electron husks have 19-25 nodes (Claude 19, Notion 19, Antigravity 22, Discord 25), 77-88% unnamed, and 0 named nodes inside the webarea (Antigravity 2). Browsers have 51-56 nodes (49-50% unnamed) because the Views chrome is shallow. Offscreen husk nodes are all zero-height: Discord 1 (1248x0), Claude 2 (600x0), Antigravity 6 (2560x0/1x0), Brave 4 (1021x0/0x0), Chrome 1 (330x0). Frontier nodes number 2-9 and carry only RightClick+ScrollTo in Electron.
exceptions: Firefox (Gecko) and YT Music (WebKit web app) also hit the depth-10 frontier but don't have the 7-node skeleton, so the frontier rule, not the skeleton, is what catches them.
deterministic_rule: If a skeleton has 7 nodes and root_kids == 4, classify the app as a Chromium shell. Skip the default-depth snapshot and go straight to --max-depth >= 30 (the forced web trees reached depth 12-30: Brave 16, Discord 25, Notion 30).

law: Native toolkits give full, trustworthy trees in the background. Foreground activation adds 0-5% of nodes and changes 0% of the text. Only web content needs depth, and nothing needs focus.
evidence: Pass-1 captures that were never activated (window not focused) vs later foreground depth-40 captures: Safari 157 -> 157 (157/157 same name+value, 157/157 same bounds), VLC 57 -> 57 (57/57 both), Calendar 170 -> 170 (169/170 text), UTM 31 -> 31 (30/31), Notes 49 -> 49 (48/49), Reminders 88 -> 88 (87/88), Music native chrome 47 (complete). Chrome's browser chrome (Views) in background: 51 nodes at depth <=10, the same as forced's 51. Native apps that were activated in pass 1 also match forced: Finder 1571 -> 1599 (1571/1571 text), TextEdit 129/129, Gemini 212 -> 222, WhatsApp 48 -> 48. The frameworks covered are AppKit, SwiftUI, Catalyst-style WhatsApp, custom C++ (Zoom 67, Word 106 -> 103) and Qt (OBS skeleton = full = 62).
exceptions: Telegram (native Swift, opaque in every mode). Keynote (launch-splash timing, see the launch law). Zoom forced (44) is a different, smaller window (w-28690 960x660 vs w-27980 1280x960), a change in window set rather than hydration.
deterministic_rule: If no webarea is present, the tree is complete=true, max depth < --max-depth, and n > 12, trust a background snapshot for reading. Do not activate the app just to read.

law: The offscreen state marks a window the user can't see (minimized or on another Space), not an unready tree. Saturated-offscreen trees are content-identical to the foreground tree.
evidence: Safari background: root.states=['offscreen'] and 157/157 nodes offscreen. In the foreground, the same window w-27784 has 51/157 offscreen, with 157/157 identical names, values and bounds. VLC: 53/57 (93%) offscreen -> 0/57 with 57/57 identical. WhatsApp: root offscreen, 5/48 -> 0/48, 46/48 identical. All 3 had a window-server entry that was only a thumbnail proxy (Safari 108x151, VLC 125x157, WhatsApp 130x96 at x=-146). Background apps with full-size window entries (Calendar, Notes, Reminders, UTM) show 0 offscreen. Big scrolled lists also saturate offscreen without being hidden: Finder is 96% offscreen in both the background (1507/1571) and the foreground (1535/1599), but has complete=false.
exceptions: Finder-style long lists (complete=false) reach >=90% offscreen through scrolling. Only a root-level offscreen state, or >=90% offscreen on a complete tree, means the window is hidden.
deterministic_rule: hidden_window := 'offscreen' in root.states OR (offscreen_nodes/n >= 0.9 AND complete == true). If hidden_window, read names and values as trusted. Activate the window before any visibility-dependent or coordinate action, then re-snapshot. This fired on 3/24 default captures (Safari, VLC, WhatsApp) and 0/21 foreground forced captures.

law: Bounds and root role belong to one snapshot. Activation or elapsed time often moves the window, which shifts every coordinate while the content stays the same, and the root role flips between dialog and window.
evidence: Same content (path + role + name matched), bounds compared: Notes 0/48 bounds equal (window moved x 780 -> 2700, to display 2), TextEdit 0/129, Reminders 0/87 (y +2px), Word 0/103, Gemini 34/209. Unchanged: Safari 157/157, VLC 57/57, Calendar 168/169, UTM 30/30, Finder 1331/1571. Root role: Calendar, Music, Notes, Reminders and UTM were 'dialog' in background pass-1 captures and 'window' in the foreground (node counts equal: 170, 47, 49, 88, 31). WhatsApp went the other way, window -> dialog (48 = 48).
exceptions: None of the moves changed names or values. Only geometry and the root role are unstable.
deterministic_rule: After any activate, open -a, or Space switch, throw away cached bounds and re-snapshot before any coordinate action. Treat root role in {window, dialog} as the same thing and never gate trust on it.

law: Enumeration-limit truncation (complete=false, nodes_observed > n) is a stable partial prefix. Recapture, activation and drilling do not fix it, so the agent should use it as it is and navigate.
evidence: Default -> forced (foreground, depth 40) delivered/observed: Finder 1571/2374 -> 1599/2417, Safari 157/229 -> 157/229, Reminders 88/102 -> 88/103, Gemini 212/220 -> 222/230, Keynote forced 689/1072. snapshot --root drills on the truncation boundary: 0 of 7 succeeded (Keynote 3/3 TIMEOUT on browser > scrollarea > list with 303 kids; Reminders 4/4 TIMEOUT down scrollarea > outline > treeitem > cell). The delivered share holds steady between captures (Finder 66% -> 66%, Reminders 86% -> 85%).
exceptions: Gemini and Safari have complete=false with no subtree_truncated marker, so the loss is somewhere not marked.
deterministic_rule: If complete == false and nodes_observed > n, trust the delivered nodes. Don't retry, activate or drill: 0/7 drills succeeded and each costs up to 45s. To reach missing items, scroll the marked container (ScrollTo / Scroll) or use in-app search, then re-snapshot.

law: Telegram's opaque root is a fixed signature that time and focus don't change. The very first capture is enough to give up on AX for this app.
evidence: 4 captures over 20.5 minutes (skeleton + full at 21:03:49 background/pre-activated, forced at 21:19:11 foreground depth 40, forced_warm at 21:24:24 foreground after a 17s settle) are byte-for-byte the same shape. Each has 1 node: role window, states ['focused'], subtree_truncated true, ax_identifier '_NS:13', bounds 1087x803, complete=false, nodes_observed=1, ref_count=0, data.truncated=true. list-surfaces returns APP_UNRESPONSIVE, kind surface_array_incomplete, attribute AXChildren, total_count 56, loaded_count 0, count_changed false. No other app among 24 has n=1 or ref_count=0.
exceptions: None observed. The agent-desktop source marks renderer probe failures as retryable, but for Telegram 4 attempts loaded 0 children every time.
deterministic_rule: If n == 1 AND root.subtree_truncated AND ref_count == 0, or if any read returns APP_UNRESPONSIVE with loaded_count == 0 and count_changed == false, stop using AX for this app right away. There is no ref to drill, and waiting or activating changes nothing. Switch to the app's API or vision.

law: RefMap>1MB is a tool size limit hit by a tree that is too big. Retrying the same scope, including without -i, fails the same way. The fix is to split the capture using the drillable frontier refs.
evidence: Antigravity forced: INTERNAL 'RefMap exceeds 1MB size limit on write' (crates/core/src/refs.rs serialize_with_size_check). capture_forced2.py then retried without -i, and forced.json holds that retry, which is still INTERNAL. Its depth-10 tree was 22 nodes with 5 frontier nodes, all carrying ref_id. Across the 8 web-stack default captures, 202/202 frontier nodes have a ref_id, so all can be drilled. The largest captures that succeeded: Notion 995 refs (1,074,609-byte output), YT Music 968, Finder 831.
exceptions: Scoped drilling was never actually run on Antigravity, so whether it fits under the limit is inferred, not measured.
deterministic_rule: On error.code == INTERNAL with a message containing 'RefMap', don't retry at the same scope and don't drop -i. Take a depth-10 snapshot, then run snapshot --root <ref> --snapshot <id> --max-depth 40 on each frontier ref one at a time, or step depth 10 -> 20 -> 30 and keep the largest one that succeeds.

law: window_without_accessibility_element and AMBIGUOUS_TARGET are errors about which window or process was targeted, not about whether the tree is ready. They are fixed by re-picking the target, not by waiting.
evidence: window_without_accessibility_element = ACTION_NOT_SUPPORTED with details.kind 'window_without_accessibility_element' (agent-desktop window_resolve.rs:352-358): the window exists in list-windows but has no AX element. No instance survived in the saved JSON, because capture.py overwrote pre-activation captures. However, the 3 native apps that were pushed into 'activated' mode (Finder, Gemini, TextEdit) had a recorded pre-activation best_window that was a ghost (2560x30 strip for Finder and Gemini, a 678x64 sliver for TextEdit). After activation they gave 1571/212/129-node trees within 5% of forced. AMBIGUOUS_TARGET: Firefox list-surfaces --app matched 11 same-name processes (candidate_count 11).
exceptions: The Space-switch cause is taken from code comments and ghost-window targets, not from a preserved error in this corpus.
deterministic_rule: On window_without_accessibility_element: re-run list-windows, apply the ghost filter (drop invisible, unfocused, title==app_name strips and <=200px thumbnails), and retry. If it still fails, activate and use snapshot --surface focused --app. On AMBIGUOUS_TARGET: pick the candidate pid that owns the target window, and always address snapshots by --window-id, never by --app name.

law: The one real timing hazard is the launch transient. A just-launched app can show a small temporary window that is later replaced by a different window id. The 12-node floor catches it.
evidence: Keynote in pass 2 (after the process appeared: 6s settle, open -a, 2s): a 9-node window w-28256 (910x608, focused). 15 minutes later, forced gave a different window, w-28758 (891x448), with 689 nodes (76.6x), mostly the template list. Zoom: default window w-27980 1280x960 had 67 nodes with a webarea; forced window w-28690 960x660 had 44 nodes and no webarea. The window set changed, but neither tree was wrong. By contrast, the 6 web apps compared at depth <=10 gained 0-3 nodes over about 12-15 extra minutes, and Telegram gained 0 over 20.5 minutes including a 17s warm settle. Extra settle time helped only in the launch case.
exceptions: Only one clear case (Keynote). Other iWork and Office apps weren't captured mid-launch.
deterministic_rule: After launching, list windows twice about 2s apart. Proceed only when the best window id is stable and the snapshot has n > 12. If n <= 12 and the root is not opaque, wait 2s, re-list, activate, and recapture once. If it is still <= 12, fall back to non-AX.

law: Readiness ladder: a fixed order of checks that sends every capture in the corpus to 'trust', 'recapture deeper', 'navigate the partial tree', 'activate first' or 'give up' in at most 2 snapshots.
evidence: Replaying the ladder on the 24 default full.json captures: TRUST 8 (Calendar, Word, Music, Notes, OBS, TextEdit, UTM, Zoom). R4 depth-frontier 8 (Antigravity, Brave, Claude, Discord, Chrome, Firefox, Notion, YT Music); after the depth-40 recapture, 7/8 reach TRUST and Antigravity goes to the RefMap branch. R5 partial-prefix 4 (Finder, Gemini, Reminders, Safari). R6 hidden-window 3 (Safari, VLC, WhatsApp), all TRUST in the foreground. R3 unsettled 1 (Keynote, which becomes a usable R5 tree of 689 nodes). R2 opaque 1 (Telegram, which stays opaque in all 4 captures). No foreground forced capture wrongly fired R2, R3, R4 or R6.
exceptions: The handshake rung is not observed. agent-desktop sends AXManualAccessibility automatically only for a complete, above-cap tree with no webarea, and retries with 25 -> 400ms backoff. No capture here met that gate. The 'handshake + recapture' rung is therefore kept only as an automatic behavior inside the tool, not a step the caller takes.
deterministic_rule: 0) Snapshot the ghost-filtered best window by --window-id at --max-depth 10 (40 if the skeleton has 7 nodes with 4 root kids). E) If there is an error: window_without_accessibility_element -> re-pick the window, then activate + --surface focused. AMBIGUOUS_TARGET -> address by pid/window-id. INTERNAL 'RefMap' -> scoped --root drill of the frontier refs. APP_UNRESPONSIVE with loaded_count 0 -> go to R2. R2) If n == 1 and root.subtree_truncated and ref_count == 0 -> GIVE UP, use non-AX. R3) If n <= 12 -> re-list windows, activate, wait 2s, recapture once; still <= 12 -> non-AX. R4) If any children_count > len(children) or max depth == --max-depth -> recapture at depth 40 (no activation needed) and go back to R2. R5) If complete == false and nodes_observed > n -> TRUST the prefix, then scroll or search to reach the rest; never drill. R6) If the root is offscreen, or >= 90% of nodes are offscreen with complete == true -> TRUST for reading, and ACTIVATE + re-snapshot before acting. Otherwise TRUST. After any activation, invalidate cached bounds.
confidence: high for corpus replay; medium as a general algorithm
